newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 24.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard is expected to launch a strong defence of the Government's economic reforms and Australia's economic health when he addresses a business and academic audience at the Sir Robert Menzies Memorial Lecture at the Centre for Australian Studies today. One issue Howard will stress is that Australia is performing better economically than the leading industrialised nations due to the Government's pursuit of a pragmatic approach. Page 1.

The planned sell-off of shares by ICI Australia's British parent company could benefit Australian investors enormously as ICI has offered local investors a A$1.2 billion stake in the company. The details of the off-loading were announced yesterday and include a A$360 million share buyback by ICI Australia. Page 1.

The Federal Police and the Australian Securities Commission have arrested fugitive businessman Russell Goward at the Hare Krishna New Govardhana Farm near Murwillumbah on the NSW north coast. The former chief of investment firm Westmex has been remanded in custody to appear in Sydney's Central Local Court this Friday to face charges of perjury and the making of false statements. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has continued to promote taxation reform debate by calling for a crackdown on people avoiding their income tax obligations. Costello told Parliament yesterday the Government was aiming to widen Australia's income tax base and would work to ensure that "... everybody pays their fair share of income taxes". Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Former 1980s high flyer businessman Russell Goward appeared in Tweed Heads Local Court in NSW yesterday charged with breaching his bail conditions. Goward was arrested at a Hare Krishna religious commune at Murwillumbah on Saturday morning and has been on the run for three months after disappearing from his home in north Sydney. Page 1.

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser is coming under increasing pressure from the ALP over allegations that he has breached Prime Minister John Howard's ministerial code of conduct. Prosser yesterday admitted he had called Coles Myer director Nik Greiner and asked him to secure a Target store for one of his company's shopping centres. Page 1.

The Federal Government has used the threat of a double dissolution to force the ALP to backdown on Senate changes to its work-for-the-dole legislation. The Federal Government used a split between the ALP and other Senate opposition parties over the schem's compulsory element to push through its legislation. Page 1.

Australia has applauded US President Bill Clinton's for preventing the Denver Summit of Eight from setting clear goals for greenhouse gas emission reductions. Australian Government sources say the lack of agreement on binding targets was "..a positive reult for Australia". Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The ALP and the Australian Democrats have backed down on their opposition to the Federal Government's compulsory Work for the Dole scheme, passing the legislation through the Senate. The Government however is still threatening a double dissolution on the issue unless both parties abandon their support for a proposed amendment which imposes a two-year sunset clause on the scheme's duration. Page 1.

Fugitive businessman Russell Goward who jumped bail while awaiting trial for perjury and concealing assets was arrested on the weekend by Australian Federal Police at a Hare Krishna retreat near Murwillumbah on the NSW north coast. Russell was a prominent business figure in the 1980s, heading the listed investment company Westmenx Ltd before it collapsed in 1990. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has overruled an invitation issued by Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer to Palestine Liberation Organisation leader Yasser Arafat to visit Australia. Fischer made the offer during his 10-day tour of the Middle East in March and its subsequent withdrawal has offended Palestinians, with Australian PLO Delegation head Ali Kazak saying last night the diplomatic bungle reflected badly on the Australian Government. Page 1.

Mater Hospital board chairman Des Giugni has resigned in protest following a decision to replace the hospital's pastoral care team, consisting of a priest and four lay people, with a team of specialist psychologists and psychiatrists. The development has raised concerns over the provision of future spiritual guidance and care at the private hospital which is owned by the Catholic Sisters of Mercy order. Page 2.
THE AGE

The Federal ALP yesterday abandoned its opposition to the Government's work-for-the-dole scheme and voted for it in the Senate, promptly dropping its support for the sole amendment the Senate had passed to the legislation - a sunset clause requiring the scheme be reviewed after two years. The Government had threatened a double dissolution over the issue. Page 1.

Police yesterday drained a swamp in the Edward Hunter Reserve near Moe in Victoria as part of the most intensive search effort yet for missing infant Jaidyn Leskie. Today over 100 police and volunteers will search 54 hectares of bushland surrounding the swamp, acting on circumstantial evidence which suggests Jaidyn could have been taken there following his abduction. Page 1.

In a speech yesterday to a Thai-Australian Association meeting in Bangkok, James Wise, Australia's second most senior diplomat in Thailand, stated the unequivocal opposition of the Australian Government to the policies of Independent MP Pauline Hanson. Wise stressed that Hanson was not representative of Australian society and that Prime Minister John Howard had opposed her strongly in public. Page 1.

A A$25 million aquarium on the banks of the Yarra River near the Crown Casino has received the approval of the Victorian Government. Melbourne City Council claims the project will attract over 700,000 visitors annually, and will contribute to making the Yarra River corridor the cultural, entertainment and commercial heart of the city. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
